summary: NewStore returns a Store with a nil values map, so the first Set call panics with 'assignment to entry in nil map'. Criterion 1 (Set then Get returns "3", true) cannot hold; criterion 2 works because reading a nil map is safe. The only test covers the missing-key path, so the panic is never exercised.

findings.title: NewStore leaves values map nil; Set panics
findings.detail: NewStore returns &Store{} without initialising values. Store.Set then does s.values[k] = v (line 20) on a nil map, which panics at runtime. Any caller doing s := session.NewStore(); s.Set("cart", "3") crashes, so criterion 1 is not met.
findings.fix: Initialise the map in the constructor: return &Store{values: make(map[string]string)} (or lazily create it in Set under the lock).

findings.title: No test covers Set followed by Get
findings.detail: The only test checks Get on a missing key. Nothing exercises Set, which is why the nil-map panic was not caught, and criterion 1 has no test backing it.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls s := NewStore(); s.Set("cart", "3"); asserts Get("cart") returns "3", true; optionally add a concurrent Set/Get test run under -race.

criteria.evidence: store.go:13 NewStore returns &Store{} with a nil map; Set at store.go:20 assigns into it and panics, so Get("cart") can never return "3", true.
Get on a nil map returns the zero value and false (store.go:27-28); TestGetMissing asserts "" and false.
